merchant_category_code.description: List of merchant category codes; null means applies to all MCCs

possible_relationships.relationship: match if the mcc is in the list or the list is empty
lookup mcc based on merchant name

domain_knowledge: MCC (Merchant Category Code) is a four-digit code assigned by card networks to categorize merchant business type, following ISO 18245 standard.
MCC affects payment processing rates, risk assessment, fraud detection, and accounting.
MCC is used to determine applicable interchange rates and fee schedules.
A complete list of MCCs is available in merchant_category_codes.csv.

monthly_fraud_level.description: Range of percentage = fraudulent transactions / total transactions in a month; null means applies to all levels

possible_relationships.relationship: calculate percentage and check if within defined range

possible_formulas: monthly_fraud_rate = sum(has_fraudulent_dispute == 'True') / count(*) over month by merchant
domain_knowledge: Fraud level is the ratio of fraudulent volume to total volume, measured monthly.
Higher fraud rates increase processing costs and may trigger account review or penalties.
Maintaining low fraud levels is essential to minimize fees and avoid penalties.
Best practices include using AVS, CVV, 3D Secure, and risk engines to reduce fraud.

monthly_volume.description: Range of total transaction amount in a month per merchant; null means applies to all volumes

possible_relationships.relationship: aggregate monthly total and check if within range

possible_formulas: monthly_volume = sum(eur_amount) over month by merchant
domain_knowledge: Monthly transaction volume per merchant determines eligibility for tiered pricing models.
Higher volumes typically result in lower per-transaction fees due to economies of scale.
No minimum volume is required, but larger volumes flatten the pricing curve for better rates.

is_credit.description: Boolean: true if payment is by credit card; null means applies to all

possible_relationships.relationship: convert both into boolean and match the value

domain_knowledge: Credit card transactions often incur higher interchange and processing fees than debit.
Fee rules may specifically target credit transactions for higher rates.

intracountry.description: 1.0 if issuing_country == acquirer_country, else 0.0; null means applies to all

possible_relationships.relationship: compare to get the boolean value

domain_knowledge: Intracountry (domestic) transactions occur when issuing and acquiring countries are the same.
Local acquiring reduces transaction friction, improves conversion, and lowers fees.
Cross-border payments may incur additional fees, currency conversion, and compliance checks.

aci.data_type: list of strings or empty list
aci.description: List of ACI codes; empty means applies to all

possible_relationships.relationship: match if the aci is in the list or the list is empty

domain_knowledge: ACI (Authorization Characteristics Indicator) categorizes transaction authentication and flow.
Different ACI codes reflect card presence, authentication method, and risk level.
Choosing the right ACI can optimize fees and reduce transaction friction.

account_type.data_type: list of strings or empty list
account_type.description: List of account types; empty means applies to all

possible_relationships.relationship: match if the account_type is in the list or the list is empty
lookup account_type based on merchant name

domain_knowledge: Account type classifies merchants by business model (e.g., Retail, Digital, Hospitality, Franchise, SaaS, Other).
Account type impacts fee schedules, settlement times, and support services.
See manual.md for account type definitions.

capture_delay.description: Range of integers (e.g., '<3', '3-5') or string (e.g., 'manual'); null means applies to all

possible_relationships.relationship: if range, check if capture_delay falls within range; if not, exact match

domain_knowledge: Capture delay is the time from authorization to settlement (e.g., '<3', '3-5', 'immediate', 'manual').
Faster capture (shorter delay) may increase fees but improves cash flow.
Late settlement can cause transaction downgrades and higher costs.
